transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-03-13
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Ortega (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Harbor Payments - Head of Payments), Samir Patel (Harbor - DevOps), Priya Nair (Harbor - Security)

Summary:
- Renewal coming up in May; customer evaluating capacity upgrade to 3 regions and dedicated reserved pool to handle seasonal peak.
- Security team needs SOC 2 artifacts, network diagrams, and KMS/HSM details for contract extension.
- SE to run benchmark for Harbor's peak workload; AE to send pricing and revised SOW for committed capacity.

Topics:
- Renewal timeline and contract length (1 vs 3 year)
- Dedicated capacity sizing and multi-region deployment
- Network/VPC options, encryption, KMS, audit logs
- Benchmarks/latency goals and cost tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Um, quick roll call then we'll dive in. I'm Maya, AE on the account, Daniel from eng is with me.
[00:12] Lena: Hi, Lena here. Samir and Priya from our infra and security teams are on too.
[00:18] Samir: Yep, Samir. Good to be here.
[00:21] Daniel: Hello, thanks.
[00:24] Maya: Great. So main purpose — renewal's in May — wanted to talk through expansion ask: Harbor's seeing a 2.5x peak in holiday windows and you mentioned wanting dedicated capacity across US-East, US-West, and EU-West, correct, Lena?
[00:38] Lena: Yeah that's right. Our product leads want predictable latency for checkout flows and also data residency for EU customers. We're considering upgrading to a reserved Dedicated pool rather than hosted.
[00:48] Maya: Understood. A couple quick Qs before Daniel goes into perf details — what's the current average qps and your peak?
[00:55] Samir: Right now baseline about 12k requests per minute, peak last month ~850k tokens and roughly 500 RPS sustained for an hour, but holiday spikes could hit 1.2k RPS.
[01:10] Daniel: Ok that maps. For 1.2k RPS with our 8xA100-style profiles you'd be looking at a small cluster of dedicated workers with autoscale headroom; exact count depends on batch size and sequence lengths.
[01:24] Priya: From security: we need SOC 2 type II, network diagrams, SAML SSO certs, and how you do key management — KMS, HSM — and if logs are retained for 365 days.
[01:37] Maya: Yes. We'll include SOC 2 reports and a network diagram in the security pack. On KMS — we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or HSM integration for Private deployments; for Dedicated we'll show options and rotation policies. Logs retention is configurable, and audit logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[01:54] Priya: Great, can you include details about inter-region traffic encryption and whether the private control plane ever surfaces data?
[02:03] Daniel: Short answer: control plane metadata doesn't contain raw customer prompts; for private we can run a customer-managed control plane. Inter-region traffic is TLS and can be VPC-peered for private routes. I'll send the network path diagram and call out egress flows.
[02:18] Lena: Thanks. On capacity — are we looking at committed spend? Our finance prefers a committed contract to hit a lower per-token and reserved instance rate.
[02:27] Maya: Yes, committed capacity is how we get predictable unit economics. We have monthly reserved clusters with commit tiers; typical customers go 12 or 36 month to get the best rates. Do you have a target budget range for committed spend?
[02:40] Lena: We can do a rough range — $250k to $600k annually depending on discounts. Also interested in the ability to add regions mid-term.
[02:50] Maya: You can add regions, it's a configuration we include in the SOW, and we can offer a phased rollout to limit upfront cost. We'll model a 3-region commit vs a 1-region with burst.
[03:02] Daniel: For the benchmarking, we want to simulate your peak patterns — continuous 30-minute bursts at 1.2k RPS and some tail spikes. We'll also test with your typical prompt lengths; longer sequences change memory/KV cache behavior and kernel selection.
[03:17] Samir: One thing — our infra team manages K8s and we'd like to know the footprint if we decide on Private on-prem. How many GPUs per rack, etc?
[03:25] Daniel: For Private on-prem, typical density is 8–16 GPUs per rack depending on SKU; we'll send a hardware spec sheet. Note that Dedicated removes the onus of hardware ops but Private gives you full control.
[03:36] Lena: If we do Dedicated, can we schedule maintenance windows? Our checkout traffic is sensitive.
[03:41] Maya: Absolutely. Dedicated has configurable maintenance windows and blackout times. Also we have SLA credits for unplanned downtime per the contract.
[03:48] Priya: A few compliance questions about data residency — when requests route to EU, are logs stored in region or replicated?
[03:56] Daniel: We can configure logs and vector stores to be region-bound. By default we place storage near compute but we can restrict replication; that'll be in the SOW & deployment config.
[04:07] Lena: Great. Another cost question — the tradeoff between latency and cost with batching? We need sub-200ms p95 for short checkout prompts.
[04:16] Daniel: Batching helps cost per token but increases latency. For sub-200ms p95 you'd use smaller batch windows, prefix caching for repeat prompts, and more workers. We can give you recommendations — e.g., use continuous KV caching for session flows and small batch sizes for checkout route.
[04:31] Samir: Do you support model quantization? We tried some quantized variants with other vendors and saw degraded quality for some prompts.
[04:39] Daniel: Yes, we support quantized runtimes and provide model profiles — some models quantize better than others. We'll run evals on your prompt set during the benchmark to measure quality regressions.
[04:50] Maya: One more on contract length — many customers lock in 36 months for biggest discount but we can do a 12-month with a renewal T&Cs that allow expansion. Any preference?
[04:59] Lena: Probably 12 for now; we want flexibility since usage could change after the next product launch.
[05:05] Maya: Sounds fair. We'll provide both 12- and 36-month pricing in the quote.
[05:10] Priya: On SSO, we need SAML integration and SCIM provisioning. Is that supported?
[05:15] Maya: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning are supported; I'll add the integration guide to the security packet.
[05:21] Samir: For the benchmark, can you run it from our VPC peering? We prefer the traffic to originate from our network so egress measurements are accurate.
[05:30] Daniel: We can run the sim from a peered test environment or from Redwood's env — peered is better for e2e latency measurements. We'll need IAM creds and a dedicated test queue.
[05:38] Samir: Ok we'll set that up.
[05:40] Maya: Alright, quick recap of action items shortly — Daniel, anything else to add about perf testing?
[05:45] Daniel: We'll include tail latency, throughput, KV-cache hit rates, and cost per 1M tokens. Also will include notes about kernel selection and memory footprint; there may be small mis-typing in the doc, but it's fine.
[05:59] Lena: How soon can we get a test plan?
[06:02] Daniel: I'll aim to have a plan by 2026-03-19 and start tests the week of the 23rd if that works.
[06:09] Maya: Great. Pricing doc and SOW by 2026-03-16 from me. Security pack same day. Follow-up call 2026-03-20 to finalize.
[06:20] Priya: One more Q — backup/retention policies for model logs, how long are prompt texts retained?
[06:27] Daniel: Retention is configurable. For Hosted API we default to 30 days but for Dedicated/Private you can set retention to zero or 365 depending on policy; we can support redaction pipelines too.
[06:38] Samir: Good. In the last provider we had an issue where keys were rotated and it caused brief outages — how do you do key rotation without downtime?
[06:47] Maya: We support staged key rotation with dual-key acceptance windows and health checks; for Private we can accommodate your rotation cadence.
[06:55] Lena: About adding regions mid-contract — is pricing pro-rated?
[06:59] Maya: Typically pro-rated for the remainder of the term, yes. We'll show the math in the quote.
[07:05] Daniel: Also a note: if you add EU region and pin model weights to a smaller quantized variant, you might save 20–30% in unit cost but need evals for quality.
[07:14] Lena: Ok. Anything else from the Redwood side?
[07:17] Maya: No, that's it. We'll get the package over.
[07:20] Priya: Thanks.
[07:22] Maya: Before we close, can we set acceptance criteria for the pilot? We typically ask for: 1) p95 latency for checkout under 200ms; 2) stable throughput at 1.2k RPS for 30 minutes; 3) zero data exfiltration and SOC 2 artifacts provided.
[07:36] Lena: That seems reasonable. We'll confirm in email.
[07:40] Maya: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[07:45] [00:07:45 end]

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K V cache" for KV cache) and auto- punctuation artifacts consistent with meeting transcription. Links shared during call: Pricing deck (link), Security pack (link), Benchmark template (link).
